rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstratives point to this surah’s verses, and al-kitāb here means the surah; its verses are manifest in their challenge to Arab eloquence.
rows.anchor: هذه الصورة والكتاب المبين السورة أى تلك الآيات التى انزلت اليك فى هذه السورة آيات السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers two further senses of manifest: reflection shows the verses come from God rather than humans, or their Arabic makes their meanings clear to Arabs.
rows.anchor: الواضحة التى لا تشتبه على العرب معانيها لنزولها بلسانهم أو قد أبين فيها ما سألت عنه اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah may clarify what the Jews asked about Joseph’s story and Jacob’s family moving from Syria to Egypt.
rows.anchor: قد أبين فيها ما سألت عنه اليهود من قصة يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jewish scholars reportedly told the polytheists to ask Muhammad why Jacob’s family moved from Syria to Egypt and about Joseph.
rows.anchor: فقد روى أن علماء اليهود قالوا للمشريكن سلوا محمد لم انتقل آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book containing Joseph’s story was sent down in Arabic; Quran can name part of the revelation because it is a generic name for the whole or a part.
rows.anchor: أنزلنا هذا الكتاب الذى فيه قصة يوسف عليه السلام فى حال كونه قرآنا عربيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that people understand the Quran’s meanings; had it been non-Arabic, they would have objected that its verses were not made clear.
rows.anchor: لكى تفهموا معانيه ولو جعلناه قرآنا أعجميا لقالوا لولا فصلت آياته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains al-qāṣṣ as the narrator who recounts a story truthfully.
rows.anchor: والقاص الذى يأتى بالقصة على حقيقتها عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qaṣaṣ can be a verbal noun, yielding the best recounting, or a passive noun, yielding the best narrated story.
rows.anchor: وقيل القصص يكون مصدرا بمعنى الاقتصاص تقول قص الحديث يقصه قصصا ويكون فعلا بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the verbal-noun reading, the construction means the best manner of recounting; the phrase introduced by revelation supplies the omitted specific object.
rows.anchor: ﴿ نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص ﴾ نبين لك أحسن البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran recounts Joseph’s story in a uniquely artful, wondrous style unlike the accounts in earlier books.
rows.anchor: فانك لا ترى اقتصاصه فى كتب الاولين مقاربا لاقتصاصه فى القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-qaṣaṣ means the narrated material, this is the finest account because it contains unmatched lessons, wisdom, and wonders.
rows.anchor: وان اريد بالقصص المقصوص فمعناه نحن نقص عليك أحسن ما يقص من الأحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The superlative is contextual: Joseph’s story is best in its subject, as someone may be called the most learned in a particular field.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه أحسن ما يقتص فى بابه كما يقال فلان أعلم الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣ derives from following a trace, since a storyteller follows what he remembers bit by bit.
rows.anchor: واشتقاق القصص من قص اثره إذا تبعه لأن الذى يقص الحديث يتبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in min qablihi refers to the revelation; before it came, Muhammad was among those unaware of this account.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإن كنت من قبله ﴾ الضمير يرجع إلى ما أوحينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In wa-in, in is lightened from the emphatic particle, and the lām distinguishes it from negation.
rows.anchor: أن مخففة من الثقيلة واللام فارقة بينها وبين النافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is an appositional inclusion from the best story because the time contains the story; alternatively, remember when Joseph spoke.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من أحسن القصص لأن الوقت مشتمل على القصص أو التقدير اذكر إذ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf is Hebrew, not Arabic: if Arabic, its proper-name status would be its only cause preventing declension.
rows.anchor: اسم عبرانى لا عربى إذ لو كان عريبا نصرف لخلوه عن سبب آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In يا أبت, the feminine t replaces the possessive yāʾ; both are final additions, and the t becomes hāʾ at pause.
rows.anchor: أبت شامى وهى تاء تأنيث عوضت عن ياء الاضافة لتناسبهما لأن كل واحدة منهما زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Shami reading has kasra on the t; the fatḥa reading deletes the alif of يا أبتا but preserves its preceding vowel, like dropping yāʾ in يا غلام.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يا أبت ﴾ أبت شامى وهى تاء تأنيث عوضت عن ياء الاضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s seeing is a dream, not waking sight; رؤيا is restricted to what is seen in sleep.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إني رأيت ﴾ من الرؤيا لا من الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is said to have given names for the eleven stars: Jaryān, al-Dhayyāl, al-Ṭāriq, Qābis, ʿAmūdān, al-Fulayq, al-Muṣbiḥ, al-Ṣurūḥ, al-Fargh, Waththāb, and Dhū al-Kitfayn.
rows.anchor: أسماؤها ببيان النبى عليه السلام جريان والذيال والطارق وقابس وعمودان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are Joseph’s parents, or his father and maternal aunt; the stars are his brothers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والشمس والقمر ﴾ هما أبواه أو أبوه وخالته والكواكب إخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction may mean the stars were seen together with the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: قيل الواو بمعنى مع أى رأيت الكواكب مع الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars take the rational plural pronoun because they are described with prostration, an action specific to rational beings.
rows.anchor: وأجريت مجرى العقلاء فى ﴿ رأيتهم لي ساجدين ﴾ لأنه وصفها بما هو المختص بالعقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision is repeated because the first seeing concerns the bodies and the second their state; alternatively, the second clause answers an implied question about how he saw them.
rows.anchor: وكررت الرؤيا لأن الاولى تتعلق بالذات والثانية بالحال أو الثانة كلام مستأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sajidin means bowing humbly to Joseph.
rows.anchor: رأيتهم لى ساجدين أى متواضعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph was twelve; forty or eighty years passed between his dream and his brothers coming to him.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن اثنتى عشر سنة يومئذ وكان بين رؤيا يوسف ومصير اخوته إليه أربعون سنة أو ثمانون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafs reads يا بني with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال يا بني ﴾ بالفتح حيث كان حفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruʾyā here means a dream, unlike ruʾya, which can mean waking sight; the paired forms differ by feminine endings.
rows.anchor: هى بمعنى الرؤية إلا أنها مختصة بما كان منها فى المنام دون اليقظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is the answer to a prohibition: if Joseph tells them, they will scheme against him.
rows.anchor: جواب النهى أى أن قصصتها عليهم كادوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob understood that God would choose Joseph for prophethood and honor him in both abodes, so he feared his brothers’ envy.
rows.anchor: عرف يعقوب عليه السلام أن الله يصطفيه للنبوة وينعم عليه بشرف الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in yakīdū laka reflects an implied verb meaning to contrive against him and intensifies the threat compared with yakīdūnī; the verbal noun kydan adds emphasis.
rows.anchor: وانما لم يقل فيكيدوك كما قال فيكيدونى لأنه ضمن معنى فعل يتعدى باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is openly hostile and incites people to envy and plot.
rows.anchor: وهو ﴿ كيدا إن الشيطان للإنسان عدو مبين ﴾ ظاهر العداوة فيحملهم على الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream points to the same divine choosing that will be granted to Joseph; ijtabā means to select, from gathering something for oneself.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وكذلك ﴾ ومثل ذلك الاجتباء الذى دلت عليه رؤياك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuʿallimuka begins a new clause outside the comparison: God will teach Joseph the interpretation of dreams, which means their explanation or expression.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويعلمك ﴾ كلام مبتدأ غير داخل فى حكم التشبيه كأنه قيل وهو يعلمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl al-aḥādīth may mean dream interpretation, interpretation of prophetic reports, or the books of God; Joseph was the best interpreter of dreams.
rows.anchor: أى تأويل الرؤيا وتأويلها عبارتها وتفسيرها وكان يوسف أعبر الناس للرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥādīth is a collective noun for ḥadīth, not a plural of uḥdūtha.
rows.anchor: وهو اسم جمع للحديث وليس بجمع احدوثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the blessing on Jacob’s family joins worldly blessing with the afterlife: they were prophets and rulers, then received high ranks in Paradise.
rows.anchor: بأن وصل لهم نعمة الدنيا بنعمة الآخرة أى جعلهم أنبياء فى الدنيا وملوكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āl Yaʿqūb includes his descendants and others; āl derives from ahl, is reserved for people of stature, and is not used for someone lowly such as a barber.
rows.anchor: و آل يعقوب اهله وهم نسله وغيرهم واصل آل أهل بدليل تصغيره على أهيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob inferred that Joseph and his brothers would become prophets from the stars’ light, which explains the mention of Jacob’s family.
rows.anchor: وانما علم يعقوب أن يوسف يكون نبيا واخوته انبياء استدلالا بضوء الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forefathers are Abraham, the grandfather, and Isaac, the great-grandfather; they are appositional explanations of the two ancestors.
rows.anchor: أراد الجد و أبا الجد ﴿ إبراهيم وإسحاق ﴾ عطف بيان لأبويك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is knowing of those fit for selection and wise in placing matters where they belong.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن ربك عليم ﴾ يعلم من يحق له الاجتباء ﴿ حكيم ﴾ يضع الأشياء مواضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in Joseph and his brothers’ story are indications of God’s power and wisdom; Makki reads the singular āya.
rows.anchor: ﴿ آيات ﴾ علامات ودلالات على قدرة الله وحكمته فى كل شيء آية مكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is a sign for those asking about it and proof of Muhammad’s prophethood to the Jews who asked, since he told it without hearing it or reading a book.
rows.anchor: و آيات على نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم للذين سألوه من اليهود عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tafsir names Joseph’s ten half-brothers, their mother Leah, and the two sons of the maidservants Zilpah and Bilhah; after Leah died Jacob married Rachel, who bore Benjamin and Joseph.
rows.anchor: وأسماهم يهوذا وروبين وشمعون ولاوى وزبولون ويشجر وامهم ليا بنت ليان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening lām emphasizes and confirms their claim that their father’s greater love for Joseph and Benjamin is beyond doubt.
rows.anchor: اللام لام الابتداء وفيها تأكيد وتحقيق لمضمون الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Benjamin Joseph’s brother although all are brothers because Joseph and Benjamin shared a mother.
rows.anchor: و إنما قالوا واخوه وهم إخوته أيضا لأن امهما كانت واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afaʿal does not distinguish number or gender in this use; distinction is required with the definite article, while both forms are possible in an annexation.
rows.anchor: وإنما قيل أحب فى الاثنين لأن أفعل من لا يفرق فيه بين الواحد وما فوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw is circumstantial: although the two boys are small and helpless, the ten brothers are capable and useful, so they think they merit more love.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من الفرق مع لام التعريف و إذا أضيف ساع الامران والواو فى ﴿ ونحن عصبة ﴾ للحال أى أنه يفضلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUṣba means ten or more; their charge of clear error concerns worldly management, since accusing Jacob of religious error would make them unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولو وصفوه بالضلالة فى الدين لكفروا والعصبة العشرة فصاعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal to kill Joseph is presented as the group’s consensus except for the one who later says not to kill him; some say Shimon proposed it and the others assented.
rows.anchor: على ذلك إلا من قال لا تقتلوا يوسف وقيل الآمر بالقتل شمعون والبقاون كانوا راضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arḍan is an indefinite, remote place away from habitation; its vagueness is why it is used as an adverbial of unspecified place.
rows.anchor: منكورة مجهولة بعيدة عن العمران وهو معنى تنكيرها واخلائها عن الوصف ولهذا الإبهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yakhlu lakum wajhu abīkum means their father will turn wholly toward them; face pictures his attention, though wajh can also mean the person himself.
rows.anchor: يقبل عليكم إقبالة واحدة لا يلتفت عنكم إلى غيركم والمراد سلامة محبته لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense of face as the person is also found in the verse about the face of God enduring.
rows.anchor: وجاز أن يراد بالوجه الذات كما قال ويبقى وجه ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takūnū is jussive, coordinated with yakhlu; min baʿdihi means after Joseph is removed by death or exile, or after the proposed act of killing or casting him away.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتكونوا ﴾ مجزوم عطفا على يخل لكم ﴿ من بعده ﴾ من بعد يوسف أى من بعد كفايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may mean they will repent of what they did to Joseph, or become better in their father’s eyes.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قوما صالحين ﴾ تائبين إلى الله مما جنيتم عليه أو يصلح حالكم عند أبيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker was Judah, whom the tafsir describes as having the best opinion of Joseph among the brothers.
rows.anchor: هو يهوذا وكان أحسنهم فيه رأيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judah rejects killing because murder is a grave matter and proposes putting Joseph in the well’s hidden depth, where travelers might find him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا تقتلوا يوسف ﴾ فإن القتل عظيم ﴿ وألقوه في غيابة الجب يلتقطه ﴾ فى قعر البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayāba is the well’s part hidden from view; some Medinan readers use the plural ghiyābāt in the following occurrence.
rows.anchor: فى قعر البئر وما غاب منه عن عين الناظر غيابات وكذا ما بعده مدنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sayyāra means some group of people traveling the road; if you intend to act on him is the proposal’s condition.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يلتقطه بعض السيارة ﴾ بعض الأقوام الذى يسيرون فى الطريق ﴿ إن كنتم فاعلين ﴾ به شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers claim they want Joseph’s good and feel concern for him, using this to lower Jacob’s guard after deciding to plot against him.
rows.anchor: ونحن نريد له الخير ونشفق عليه وأرادوا بذلك لما عزموا على كيد يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea shows Jacob had already sensed something that made him unwilling to trust them with Joseph.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه أحس منهم بما اوجب أن لا يامنهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yartaʿ means to enjoy abundance, including eating fruit; al-ratʿa means spacious plenty.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أرسله معنا غدا يرتع ﴾ نتسع فى أكل الفواكه وغيرها والرتعة السعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Play means permissible recreation such as hunting, archery, and riding.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويلعب ﴾ نتفرج بما يباح كالصيد والرمى والركض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinan and Kufan readers use the yāʾ forms for both verbs; Makkan, Shami, and Abu ʿAmr use nūn; Hijazi readers vocalize the ʿayn with kasra.
rows.anchor: الياء فيهما مدنى وكوفى وبالنون فيهما مكى وشامى و أبو عمرو وبكسر العين حجازى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their assurance means they will protect Joseph from harm.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإنا له لحافظون ﴾ من أن يناله مكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in layahzununī is emphatic; Jacob says Joseph’s going with them would grieve him because he could not bear to be apart from him.
rows.anchor: أى يحزننى ذهابكم به واللام لام الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob fears a wolf may attack while they are distracted by tending or playing.
rows.anchor: و أنه يخاف عليه من عدوة الذئب إذا غفلوا عنه برعيهم ولعبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in la-in introduces an oath whose unstated wording is by God; the wāw in wa-naḥnu ʿuṣba marks their combined strength and ability to defend.
rows.anchor: اللام موطئة للقسم والقسم محذوف تقديره والله لئن أكله الذئب والواو فى ﴿ ونحن عصبة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s answer stands in place of the conditional response: if they could not protect one of their group, their livestock would be lost and they would be losers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنا إذا لخاسرون ﴾ جواب للقسم مجزىء عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer Jacob’s second excuse but ignore the first because it would anger them.
rows.anchor: واجابوا عن عذره الثانى دون الأول لأن ذلك كان يغيظهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well was three farsakhs from Jacob’s home; the omitted response to when they took Joseph is that they did to him what follows.
rows.anchor: وهى بئر على ثلاثة فراسخ من منزل يعقوب عليه السلام وجواب لما محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says they showed hostility in the wilderness, beat Joseph, and nearly killed him until Judah stopped them; they stripped and bound him, lowered him into a watery well, and Judah brought him food as he wept on a rock.
rows.anchor: فقد روى أنهم لما برزوا به إلى البرية أظهروا له العداوة وضربوه وكادوا يقتلونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report traces Joseph’s shirt from Gabriel, who brought it from Paradise for Abraham when he was stripped before the fire; it passed through Isaac and Jacob, who hung it as an amulet on Joseph, and Gabriel later dressed him in it.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام حين ألقى فى النار جرد عن ثيابه فاتاه جبريل عليه السلام بقميص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation to Joseph may have come in childhood, as with John and Jesus, or he may already have been mature.
rows.anchor: قيل اوحى إليه فى الصغر كما اوحى إلى يحيى وعيسى عليهما السلام وقيل كان إذ ذاك مدركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises that Joseph will tell his brothers what they did, while they fail to recognize that he is Joseph because of his later status and power.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا ﴾ أى لتحدثن إخوتك بما فعلوا بك ﴿ وهم لا يشعرون ﴾ انك يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when the brothers later came to buy provisions, Joseph recognized them; he tapped a cup that seemed to tell him they had thrown him in the well, blamed a wolf, and sold him cheaply.
rows.anchor: فعرفهم وهم له منكرون دعا بالصواع فوضعه على يده ثم نقره فطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the brothers’ unawareness describes the revelation itself: God comforted Joseph and removed his loneliness without their knowing.
rows.anchor: أو يتعلق وهم لا يشعرون بأوحينا أى آنسناه بالوحى وازلنا عن قلبه الوحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A caravan traveling from Midian to Egypt arrived three days after Joseph was thrown in the well; having lost its way, it camped nearby in an uninhabited wilderness.
rows.anchor: رفقة تسير من قبل مدين إلى مصر وذلك بعد ثلاثة أيام من إلقاء يوسف فى الجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well’s water was salty but became sweet when Joseph was cast into it.
rows.anchor: وكان ماؤه ملحا فعذب حين ألقى فيه يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water drawer was Malik ibn Dhuʿar al-Khuzaʿi; Joseph caught the bucket and was pulled out.
rows.anchor: هو الذى يرد الماء ليستقى للقوم اسمه مالك بن ذعر الخزاعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufans call out yā bushrā, as if summoning the moment of good news; others read bushrāya, attributing it to themselves, or take Bushrā as the drawer’s slave’s name.
rows.anchor: كوفى نادى البشرى كأنه يقول تعالى فهذا أوانك غيرهم بشراى على إضافتها لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drawer may have called his companions when he approached, announcing that he had found a boy.
rows.anchor: قيل ذهب به فلما دنا من أصحابه صاح بذلك يبشرهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in asarrūhu may refer to the drawer and caravan, who hid Joseph from the group, or to his brothers, who falsely called him their runaway slave and sold him; Joseph kept silent for fear they would kill him.
rows.anchor: الضمير للوارد وأصحابه اخفوه من الرفقة أو لإخوة يوسف فإنهم قالوا للرفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍāʿatan is a circumstantial accusative meaning they hid him as merchandise; biḍāʿa is a portion of wealth set aside for trade.
rows.anchor: حال أى اخفوه متاعا للتجارة والبضاعة ما بضع من المال للتجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the brothers’ wrongdoing toward both Joseph and their father.
rows.anchor: بما يعمل اخوة يوسف بأبيهم وأخيهم من سوء الصنيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharawhu means they sold him; bakhs is a visibly undervalued price or counterfeit money.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وشروه ﴾ وباعوه ﴿ بثمن بخس ﴾ مبخوس ناقص عن القيمة نقصانا ظاهرا أو زيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dirāhima is appositional to price; the coins were few and counted rather than weighed, since amounts below forty were counted and forty or more weighed; the price was twenty dirhams.
rows.anchor: ﴿ دراهم ﴾ بدل من ثمن ﴿ معدودة ﴾ قليلة تعد عدا ولا توزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may be called disinterested because they readily sold what was in their hands for a paltry price.
rows.anchor: ممن يرغب عما فى يده فيبيعه بالثمن الطفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the caravan bought Joseph from his brothers and did not value him because they thought he was a runaway slave.
rows.anchor: أو معنى وشروه واشتروه يعنى الرفقة من أخوته وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين أى غير راغبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the brothers followed the caravan and told them to secure Joseph so he would not escape; the phrase about being disinterested is explanatory, not syntactically attached to the preceding relative clause.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن اخوته اتبعوهم وقالوا استوثقوا منه لا يأبق ليس من صلة الزاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The buyer was Qitfir, the Aziz in charge of Egypt’s treasuries; the king was Rayyan ibn al-Walid, who believed in Joseph and died while Joseph lived.
rows.anchor: هو قطفير وهو العزيز الذى كان على خزائن مصر والملك يومئذ الريان بن الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account dates Joseph’s purchase at age seventeen, his thirteen years in the household, appointment as minister at thirty, wisdom and knowledge at thirty-three, and death at 120.
rows.anchor: وهو ابن سبع عشرة سنة وأقام فى منزله ثلاث عشرة سنة واستوزره ريان بن الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife is named Rael or Zulaikha; the lām in li-imraʾatihi attaches to qāla, not to the purchase verb.
rows.anchor: راعيل أو زليخا واللام متعلقة بقال لاباشتراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akrimī mathwāhu means make his dwelling and standing with us honorable and pleasant, as Joseph later says the master made his dwelling good.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أكرمي مثواه ﴾ اجعلى منزلته ومقامه عندنا كريما أى حسنا مرضيا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the command as giving Joseph good living, soft clothing, and a comfortable bed.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك بطيب معاشه ولين لباسه ووطىء فراشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph might benefit them by learning administration and managing their affairs; or the childless Qitfir, discerning his good judgment, might adopt him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ عسى أن ينفعنا ﴾ لعله إذا تدرب وراض الامور وفهم مجاريها نستظهر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kathālika points to Joseph’s rescue and the Aziz’s affection; God then empowered him to rule and command in Egypt.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما تقدم من انجائه وعطف قلب العزيز عليه والكاف منصوب تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rescue and empowerment were so that God could teach Joseph interpretation; God prevails in carrying out His purpose, delivering Joseph despite his brothers’ plan.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث ﴾ كان ذلك الانجاء والتمكين ﴿ والله غالب على أمره ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God is sovereign over Joseph’s matter, bringing him to the outcome He intended rather than the one his brothers intended.
rows.anchor: أو على أمر يوسف بتبليغه ما أراد له دون ما أراد اخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph reached mature strength at eighteen or twenty-one.
rows.anchor: منتهى استعداد قوته وهو ثمان عشرة سنة أو إحدى وعشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him judgment and knowledge, meaning wisdom joined to action and avoidance of ignorance, or judgment among people and jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: حكمة وهو العلم مع العمل واجتناب ما يجهل فيه أو تحكما بين الناس وفقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to reward those who excel signals Joseph’s excellence and piety in the prime of his life.
rows.anchor: تنبيه على أنه كان محسنا فى عمله متقيا فى عنفوان أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman sought intercourse; murāwada conveys repeated coming and going or guileful effort to obtain something the other person will not yield.
rows.anchor: طلبت يوسف أن يواقعها والمراودة مفاعلة من راد يرود إذا جاء وذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She locked seven doors.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وغلقت الأبواب ﴾ وكانت سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayta means come or approach and is indeclinable with fatḥa; Makki reads haytu with ḍamma, as do Medinan and Shami readers; the lām makes explicit whom she addresses.
rows.anchor: هو اسم لتعال وأقبل وهو مبنى على الفتح هيت مكى بناه على الضم هيت مدنى وشامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph seeks refuge in God; rabbī means his master and owner, Qitfir, whose wife had been told to honor Joseph’s dwelling.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال معاذ الله ﴾ أعوذ بالله معاذا ﴿ أنه ﴾ أى أن الشأن والحديث ﴿ ربي ﴾ سيدى ومالكى يريد قطفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph argues that betraying Qitfir’s household would violate his kindness; zalimūn can mean traitors or adulterers.
rows.anchor: حين قال لك اكرمى مثواى فما جزاؤه أن اخونه فى أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, rabbī refers to God as the one who causes all things.
rows.anchor: أو أراد بقوله إنه ربى الله تعالى لأنه مسبب الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hammat means she resolved; Joseph’s inclination was a natural impulse accompanied by restraint, as Hasan says, or only a fleeting thought for which a person has no agency or blame, as Abu Mansur says.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهم بها ﴾ هم الطباع مع الامتناع قاله الحسن وقال الشيخ أبو منصور رحمه الله

rows.speaker: أبو منصور
rows.claim: Abu Mansur says Joseph’s inclination was a passing thought in the heart, outside human agency and blame.
rows.anchor: هم خطرة ولا صنع للعبد فيمايخطر بالقلب ولا مؤاخذة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Joseph came close to intending it, since hamma bil-amr can mean to aim at and resolve upon a matter.
rows.anchor: وقيل وهم بها وشارف أن يهم بها يقال هم بالأمر إذا قصده وعزم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to lawlā is omitted; it would have said what would have happened had Joseph not seen his Lord’s proof.
rows.anchor: وجواب ﴿ لولا أن رأى برهان ربه ﴾ محذوف أى لكان ماكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Joseph acted sexually—loosening his garment, sitting between her legs, or responding to voices and a vision of Jacob—is false.
rows.anchor: وفسرهم يوسف بأنه حل تكة سراويله وقعد بين شعبها الأربع وهى مستلقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That sexualized account conflicts with Joseph’s statement that she solicited him, the claim that God warded evil away, and his later declaration of fidelity in the husband’s absence.
rows.anchor: ويدل على بطلانه قوله هى راودتنى عن نفسى ولو كان ذلك منه أيضا لما برأ نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Joseph sinned, the text would mention his repentance as it does for Adam, Noah, Jonah, and David; instead, he remained steadfast and God praised him as purified.
rows.anchor: لذكرت توبته واستغفاره كما كان لآدم ونوح وذى النون وداود عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph resisted with the resolve of the greatest prophets, considering the proofs against the forbidden act until he earned divine praise.
rows.anchor: فعلم بالقطع أنه ثبت فى ذلك المقام وجاهد نفسه مجاهدة اولى العزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kathālika can be accusative, meaning God established Joseph in that way, or nominative, meaning the matter was like that.
rows.anchor: ومحل الكاف فى ﴿ كذلك ﴾ نصب أى مثل ذلك التثبيت ثبتناه أو رفع أى الامر مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sūʾ means betrayal of the master and al-faḥshāʾ means adultery; Joseph was among God’s purified servants.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لنصرف عنه السوء ﴾ خيانة السيد ﴿ والفحشاء ﴾ الزنا ﴿ إنه من عبادنا المخلصين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinan and Kufan readers vocalize the lām of mukhlaṣīn with fatḥa, meaning God chose them; others use kasra, meaning they chose their religion sincerely; Joseph is one of the purified servants.
rows.anchor: بفتح اللام حيث كان مدنى وكوفى أى الذين أخلصهم الله لطاعته وبكسرها غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They raced toward the door: the verb is for seeking while Joseph fled and she pursued to stop him; its preposition is omitted or the verb includes the sense of rushing.
rows.anchor: وتسابقا إلى الباب هي للطلب وهو للهرب على حذف الجار وايصال الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular door is the outer exit even though the house had several doors; as Joseph fled, the lock’s pins fell apart until he got out.
rows.anchor: ووحد الباب و إن كان جمعه فى قوله وغلقت الأبواب لأنه أراد الباب البرانى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She pulled Joseph’s shirt from behind and tore it while chasing him to prevent his escape.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وقدت قميصه من دبر ﴾ اجتذبته من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They found Qitfir approaching; she tried to clear herself and intimidate Joseph into compliance by accusing him generally of seeking harm to the household.
rows.anchor: فلما رأته احتالت لتبرئة ساحتها عند زوجها من الريبة ولتخويف يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her statement uses a negation: the only fitting penalty is prison or painful flogging; she avoids naming Joseph so the threat applies broadly and is more intimidating.
rows.anchor: ما نافية أى ليس جزاؤه إلا السجن أو عذاب أليم وهو الضرب بالسياط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says she solicited him; absent that, he would have concealed the matter and spared her exposure.
rows.anchor: ولولا ذلك لكتم عليها ولم يفضحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness was her cousin, or her maternal cousin, or a baby in the cradle; God put the testimony on a relative’s tongue to make it stronger and more convincing.
rows.anchor: هو ابن عم لها وانما القى الله الشهادة على لسان من هو من اهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His words are called testimony because they functioned as evidence confirming Joseph’s statement and disproving hers.
rows.anchor: وسمى قوله شهادة لأنه أدى مؤدى الشهادة فى أن ثبت به قول يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the shirt was torn behind, she lied and Joseph spoke truth; the implied syntax is that the witness said, if the shirt proves to be torn this way.
rows.anchor: والتقدير وشهد شاهد فقال أن كان قميصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A front tear would support her because Joseph was hurrying after her, might stumble and tear its front, or she could have torn it while pushing him away.
rows.anchor: لأنه يسرع خلفها ليلحقها فيعثر فى مقادم قميصه فيشقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indefinite qablu and duburu mean from a direction called front or back; combining future-oriented in with kāna means if it turns out his shirt was torn from behind.
rows.anchor: واما تنكير قبل ودبر فمعناه من جهة يقال لها قبل ومن جهة يقال لها دبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the shirt torn behind, Qitfir knew Joseph was innocent and his wife had lied.
rows.anchor: وعلم براءة يوسف عليه السلام وصدقه وكذبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In innahu min kaydikunna, the pronoun may refer to her accusation or to the scheme of trying to seduce men.
rows.anchor: أن قولك ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا أو إن هذا الامر وهو الاحتيال لنيل الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes her and her group; women’s subtler schemes and greater cunning let them overcome men.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من كيدكن ﴾ الخطاب لها ولأمتها ﴿ إن كيدكن عظيم ﴾ لأنهن ألطف كيدا وأعظم حيلة

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars say they fear women more than Satan, contrasting Satan’s weak scheme with women’s great scheme.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض العلماء إنى أخاف من النساء أكثر مما اخاف من الشيطان لأن الله تعالى قال إن كيد الشيطان كان ضعيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative yā is omitted because Joseph is nearby and quick-witted; this both brings him close and softens the address.
rows.anchor: حذف منه حرف النداء لأنه منادى قريب مفاطن للحديث وفيه تقريب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz tells Joseph to suppress the incident and tells Rael to seek forgiveness for her deliberate sin.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أعرض عن هذا ﴾ الامر واكتمه ولا تحدث به ثم قال لراعيل ﴿ واستغفري لذنبك إنك كنت من الخاطئين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural khāṭiʾīn is generic and includes a woman; the Aziz is mild and not jealous, since he says no more.
rows.anchor: من جملة القوم المتعمدين للذنب يقال خطىء إذا أذنب متعمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women were five: the wives of the cupbearer, baker, stablemaster, prison warden, and chamberlain.
rows.anchor: وكن خمسا امرأة الساقى وامرأة الخباز وامرأة صاحب الدواب وامرأة صاحب السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-madīna is Egypt; al-ʿazīz refers to Qitfir, while ʿazīz is the Arab term for a king.
rows.anchor: ﴿ في المدينة ﴾ فى مصر ﴿ امرأة العزيز ﴾ يردن قطفير والعزيز الملك بلسان العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niswah is a singular collective for women and is not grammatically feminine in the real sense, explaining the masculine verb; its nūn is read with kasra or ḍamma.
rows.anchor: والنسوة اسم مفرد لجمع المرأة وتأنيثها غير حقيقى ولذا لم يقل قالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatā means a male servant, and fatātī a female servant.
rows.anchor: غلامها يقال فتاى وفتاتى أى غلامى وجاريتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaghafahā ḥubban is a specification: love burned through the heart’s covering to its core; shighāf may be the heart’s membrane or a thin skin called the heart’s tongue.
rows.anchor: تمييز أى قد شغفها حبه يعنى حرق حبه شغاف قلبها حتى وصل إلى الفؤاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāl mubīn means obvious error and distance from the right way.
rows.anchor: فى خطأ وبعد عن طريق الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rael hears their backbiting; it is called makr because it happens secretly in someone’s absence, or because the women had revealed a confidence.
rows.anchor: باغتيابهن وقولهم امرأة العزيز عشقت عبدها الكنعانى ومقتها وسما الاغتياب مكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She invited them; one report says she invited forty women, including the five already named.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أرسلت إليهن ﴾ دعتهن قيل دعت أربعين امراة منهم الخمس المذكورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿtadat means she prepared, from ʿitād; muttakaʾ is something to recline on, and she staged the meal and knives to astonish them into injuring their hands.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأعتدت ﴾ وهيأت افتعلت من العتاد ﴿ لهن متكأ ﴾ ما يتكئن عليه من نمارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women ate with knives, as people in that era did; she gave each a knife and told Joseph to appear before them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وآتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا ﴾ وكانوا لا يأكلون فى ذلك الزمان إلا بالسكاكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basrans, Asim, and Hamza read the tāʾ in ukhruj with kasra; the other readers use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: بكسر التاء بصرى وعاصم وحمزة وبضمها غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akbarnahu means they greatly admired and were awed by Joseph’s striking beauty.
rows.anchor: أعظمنه وهبن ذلك الحسن الرائق والجمال الفائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s beauty is likened to a full moon among stars; his face supposedly shone on Egyptian walls, resembled Adam at creation, or derived beauty from Sarah.
rows.anchor: وكان فضل يوسف على الناس فى الحسن كفضل القمر ليلة البدر على نجوم السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes akbarnahu as menstruation; its hāʾ is pause-only, since the verb is intransitive, and menstruation marks a woman’s coming of age.
rows.anchor: وقيل أكبرن بمعنى حضن والهاء للسكت إذ لا يقال النساء قد حضنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Tayyib’s line about a beautiful woman menstruating in her private quarters appears to draw on this interpretation of akbarna.
rows.anchor: وكأن أبا الطيب اخذ من هذا التفسير قوله خف الله واستر ذا الجمال ببرقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qattaʿna means wounded their hands, just as cutting meat can mean cutting one’s own hand; they meant to cut food but were stunned and scratched themselves.
rows.anchor: كما تقول كنت أقطع اللحم فقطعت يدى تريد جرحتها أى أردن أن يقطعن الطعام الذى فى أيديهن فدهشن لما رأينه فخدشن أيديهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāshā lillāh is an expression of transcendence adapted from the exception particle ḥāshā, a preposition, and means declaring God free of deficiency.
rows.anchor: حاشا كلمة تفيد معنى التنزيه فى باب الاستثناء تقول أساء القوم حاشا زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads ḥāshā lillāh, like suqyā laka, making the lām explicit; others omit the final alif in ḥāsh lillāh.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أبى عمرو وحاشا لله نحو قولك سقيا لك كأنه قال برءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclamation declares God free of incapacity and expresses wonder at His power to create someone so beautiful.
rows.anchor: وغيره حاش لله بحذف الألف الأخيرة والمعنى تنزيه الله من صفات العجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny Joseph’s humanity because his beauty seemed extraordinary and call him a noble angel, reflecting common associations of angels with beauty and devils with ugliness.
rows.anchor: نفين عنه البشرية لغرابة جماله واثتبن له الملكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rael says Joseph is the man for whom they blamed her: had they pictured his beauty correctly, they would excuse her fascination.
rows.anchor: تقول هو ذلك العبد الكنعانى الذى صورتن فى أنفسكهن ثم لمتننى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiʿṣāma is an intensive form for powerful resistance and vigilance; her admission plainly confirms Joseph’s innocence of the alleged inclination and proof.
rows.anchor: والإستعصام بناء مبالغة يدل على الامتناع البليغ والتحفظ الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She threatens imprisonment and humiliation if Joseph will not do what she commands; the final alif substitutes for the light nun of emphasis.
rows.anchor: والضمير يرجع إلى يوسف أى ولئن لم يفعل أمرى إياه أى موجب احري ومقتضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her threat depicts Joseph as lowly with thieves and fugitives, unable to eat, drink, or sleep; she says the man who rejected silk and a princely couch will end desolate on coarse matting.
rows.anchor: ليحبسن والألف فى ﴿ وليكون ﴾ بدل من نون التأكيد الخفيفة ﴿ من الصاغرين ﴾ مع السراق والسفاك والأباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph promises to explain the food’s nature and qualities, like clarifying something obscure, and to describe what will arrive before it comes.
rows.anchor: أى لبيان ماهيته وكيفيته لأن ذلك يشبه تفسير المشكل ﴿ قبل أن يأتيكما ﴾ لما استعبراه ووصفاه بالإحسان افترض ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the prisoners recognized his excellence, he disclosed a knowledge beyond scholars and used it to introduce monotheism and make faith appealing while condemning polytheism.
rows.anchor: وجعل ذلك تخلصا إلى أن يذكر لهما التوحيد ويعرض عليهما الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He would predict the day’s food and its description; this is divinely taught foreknowledge, not divination or astrology.
rows.anchor: ويصفه لهما ويقول اليوم يأتيكما طعام من صفته كيت وكيت فيكون كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālikumā refers to the interpretation and report of unseen matters, which God revealed to Joseph.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذلكما ﴾ إشارة لهما إلى التأويل أى ذلك التأويل والإخبار بالمغيبات ﴿ مما علمني ربي ﴾ وأوحى به إلى ولم أقله عن تكهن وتنجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A learned person may describe his own expertise to someone who does not know it when his aim is to benefit the listener, not self-praise.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن العالم إذا جهلت منزلته فى العلم فوصف نفسه بما هو بصدده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about leaving the unbelieving people may be a new sentence or the reason God taught him; he never followed their creed, and they were Egyptians sharing the prisoners’ religion.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون كلاما مبتدأ و أن يكون تعليلا لما قبله أى علمنى ذلك وأوحى به إلى لأنى رفضت ملة أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph follows the monotheistic creed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; repeating their names emphasizes the lineage and shows the prisoners he belongs to a prophetic household.
rows.anchor: وهى الملة الحنيفية وتكريرهم للتوكيد وذكر الآباء ليريهما أنه من بيت النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His leaving the unbelieving creed means he never adopted it, not that he once practiced it and later abandoned it.
rows.anchor: والمراد به ترك الابتداء لا أنه كان فيه ثم تركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is not proper for the prophets to associate anything with God, whether an idol or anything else.
rows.anchor: ماصح لنا معشر الانبياء ﴿ أن نشرك بالله من شيء ﴾ أى شيء كان صنما أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That monotheism is God’s favor to the prophets and all people, but most people fail to thank Him and persist in associating partners.
rows.anchor: ثم قال ﴿ ذلك ﴾ التوحيد ﴿ من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون ﴾ فضل الله فيشركون به ولا ينتهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāḥibay al-sijn means the two residents of prison, as in companions of the Fire and companions of the Garden.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يا صاحبي السجن ﴾ يا ساكنى السجن كقوله ﴿ أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many scattered lords means competing gods and masters; Joseph’s parable contrasts worship of the one irresistible God with worship of idols.
rows.anchor: يريد التفرق فى العدد والتكاثر أى أأن تكون ارباب شتى يستعبدكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address reaches both prisoners and others who follow Egypt’s religion; what they worship besides God are names they and their ancestors gave to beings lacking divinity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما تعبدون ﴾ خطاب لهما ولمن كان على دينهما من أهل مصر ﴿ من دونه ﴾ من دون الله ﴿ إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sammaytumūhā means they named the supposed gods as such; God gave no authority for that naming.
rows.anchor: أى سميتم مالا يستحق الألوهية آلهة ثم طفقتم تعبدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment over worship and religion belongs to God, who commanded that none but He be worshiped; this is the firmly established religion supported by proofs.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن الحكم ﴾ فى أمر العبادة والدين ﴿ إلا لله ﴾ ثم بين ما حكم به فقال ﴿ أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ذلك الدين القيم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that a person remains liable to punishment for ignorance when the path to knowledge was available.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن العقوبة تلزم العبد وان جهل إذا أمكن له العلم بطريقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adghāth are confused, worthless dreams—mixed plant stalks collected into bundles—arising from inner thoughts or Satan’s whispering.
rows.anchor: أى هى أضغاث احلام أى تخاليطها وأباطيها وما يكون منها من حديث نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural intensifies the description of one dream as false, or the king may have also related other dreams; the annexation means bundles made of dreams.
rows.anchor: وانما جمع وهو حلم واحد تزايدا فى وصف الحلم بالبطلان وجاز أن يكون قد قص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The courtiers may mean they only interpret sound dreams, not false ones, or admit they lack knowledge of dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: أرادوا بالأحلام المنامات الباطلة فقالوا ليس لها عندنا تأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣiddīq means one perfected in truthfulness; the messenger calls Joseph that because his earlier interpretations of his and his companion’s dreams proved true.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يوسف أيها الصديق ﴾ أيها البليغ فى الصدق و إنما قال له ذلك لأنه ذاق وتعرف صدقه فى تأويل رؤياه ورؤيا صاحبه حيث جاءكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger asks Joseph to interpret the seven fat cows, seven lean cows, and grain vision so he can return to the king and his entourage, who may then recognize Joseph’s merit and free him.
rows.anchor: أول ﴿ أفتنا في سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات لعلي أرجع إلى الناس ﴾ إلى الملك وأتباعه ﴿ لعلهم يعلمون ﴾ فضلك ومكانك من العلم فيطلبوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālik refers to Joseph’s refusal to leave prison until his innocence was publicly established.
rows.anchor: أى امتناعى من الخروج والتثبت لظهور البرءاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king should know Joseph did not betray Qitfir regarding his wife in his absence; alternatively, the king should know Joseph did not betray the Aziz.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ليعلم ﴾ العزيز ﴿ أني لم أخنه بالغيب ﴾ بظهور الغيب فى حرمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bil-ghayb may be a circumstantial phrase describing Joseph as absent from the Aziz or the Aziz as absent from Joseph.
rows.anchor: وبالغيب حال 8 من الفاعل أو المفعول على معنى و أنا غائب عنه أو وهو غائب عنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide a traitor’s scheme means He does not make it succeed; Joseph indirectly censures the wife’s betrayal of her husband’s trust.
rows.anchor: لا يسدده و كأنه تعريض بامراته في خيانتها امانة زوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph humbles himself rather than praise himself, crediting his integrity to God’s enabling and protection; he does not claim absolute innocence.
rows.anchor: ثم اراد ان يتواضع لله ويهضم نفسه لئلا يكون لها مزكيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may deny complete innocence generally, or in this incident because of a passing human thought that involved neither intent nor resolve.
rows.anchor: ولا ازكيها فى عموم الأحوال أو فى هذه الحادثة لما ذكرنا من الهم الذى هو الخطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nafs is generic: the human self urges evil because of its desires.
rows.anchor: أراد الجنس أى ان هذا الجنس يأمر بالسوء ويحمل عليه لما فيه من الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may mean those God preserves from evil, the time of divine protection, or an independent exception meaning God’s mercy alone averts wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: إلا البعض الذى رحمه ربى بالعصمة ويجوز أن يكون ما رحم فى معنى الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some attribute these words to the Aziz’s wife: she admits that she betrayed and falsely accused Joseph, imprisoned him, and now seeks forgiveness and mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من كلام امرأة العزيز أى ذلك الذى قلت ليعلم يوسف إنى لم أخنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although no explicit marker identifies the speaker, the meaning favors Joseph; another proposal rearranges the Quranic sequence so that this statement follows his request to ask the women.
rows.anchor: و إنما جعل من كلام يوسف ولا دليل عليه ظاهر لان المعنى يقود إليه وقيل هذا من تقديم القرآن وتأخيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Astaḵliṣhu means to make Joseph exclusively close to the king; after speaking with him, the king saw more than he expected and called him established and trustworthy.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وقال الملك ائتوني به أستخلصه لنفسي ﴾ اجعله خالصا لنفسى ﴿ فلما كلمه ﴾ وشاهد منه مالم يحتسب ﴿ قال ﴾ الملك ليوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes an envoy with seventy guards and mounts and royal clothes; Joseph prayed for the prisoners, inscribed a saying over the prison gate, bathed, and put on clean clothes.
rows.anchor: روى أن الرسول جاءه ومعه سبعون حاجبا وسبعون مركبا وبعث إليه لباس الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before meeting the king Joseph asked God for good from him and protection from his evil, then greeted him in Hebrew; the king spoke seventy languages and Joseph answered in all of them.
rows.anchor: ثم اغتسل وتنظف من درن السجن ولبس ثيابا جدد فلما دخل على الملك قال اللهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asked to hear Joseph’s interpretation; Joseph described the cows, sheaves, and where they appeared, then advised storing grain in silos to feed arrivals and amass unprecedented reserves.
rows.anchor: رأيت بقرات فوصف لونهن واحوالهن ومكان خروجهن ووصف السنابل وما كان منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to govern Egypt’s storehouses; ḥafīẓ means he will faithfully guard what is entrusted to him, and ʿalīm means he knows how to administer it.
rows.anchor: ولى على خزائن أرضك يعنى مصر ﴿ إني حفيظ ﴾ أمين أحفظ ما تستحفظنيه ﴿ عليم ﴾ عالم بوجوة التصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He names trustworthiness and competence, qualities rulers seek in an appointee, so he can implement God’s judgments, establish justice, and fulfill the prophets’ mission; no one else could do it.
rows.anchor: و إنما قال ذلك ليتوصل إلى إمضاء إحكام الله وإقامة الحق وبسط العدل والتمكن مما لأجله بعث الأنبياء إلى العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph sought God’s pleasure rather than the king or worldly advantage.
rows.anchor: فطلبه ابتغاء وجه الله لا لحب الملك والدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says God have mercy on Joseph: had he not asked for the storehouses, the king would have appointed him at once, but the appointment was delayed a year.
rows.anchor: وفى الحديث رحم الله أخى يوسف لو لم يقل اجعلنى على خزائن الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports taking a post under an unjust ruler; early Muslims accepted judicial positions from tyrants.
rows.anchor: قالوا وفيه دليل على أنه يجوز أن يتولى الإنسان عمالة من يد سلطان جائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet or scholar may seek a ruler’s support when only that power can enforce God’s law and remove oppression, even if the ruler is an unbeliever or sinner.
rows.anchor: واذا علم النبي أو العالم أنه لا سبيل إلى الحكم بأمر الله ودفع الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the king submitted to Joseph’s judgment and followed him without objection.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان الملك يصدر عن رأيه ولا يعترض عليه فى كل ما رأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s similar empowerment placed Joseph in Egypt, a land forty by forty farsakhs; tamkīn means giving someone power and capacity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وكذلك ﴾ ومثل ذلك التمكين الظاهر ﴿ مكنا ليوسف في الأرض ﴾ أرض مصر وكانت أربعين فرسخا فى أربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph could settle wherever he chose because the whole land was under his authority; Makki reads nashiʾa without the final alif.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يتبوأ منها حيث يشاء ﴾ أى كل مكان أراد أن يتخذه منزلا لم يمنع منه لاستيلائه على جميعها ودخولها تحت سلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy here includes worldly gifts such as kingship and wealth, given where wisdom deems fitting.
rows.anchor: بعطائنا فى الدنيا من الملك والغنى وغيرهما من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not waste the reward of those who excel in this world.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين ﴾ فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The better reward of the Hereafter belongs to Joseph and other believers until the Resurrection, who guard themselves from idolatry and indecencies.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وكانوا يتقون ﴾ الشرك والفواحش قال سفيان بن عيينة المؤمن يثاب على حسناته فى الدنيا و الآخرة

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna says believers receive recompense for good deeds in this life and the Hereafter, while the wicked receive worldly good early and no share in the next life.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة المؤمن يثاب على حسناته فى الدنيا و الآخرة والفاجر يعجل له الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the king crowned and robed Joseph, gave him a jeweled golden throne, ring, and sword, then entrusted rule to him; Joseph rejected the crown as foreign to his family.
rows.anchor: روى أن الملك توج يوسف وختمه بخاتمة ورداه بسيفه ووضع له سريرا من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king removed Qitfir and married Joseph to Qitfir’s wife; she was a virgin, bore Ephraim and Misha, and Egypt’s king and many people accepted Islam through Joseph.
rows.anchor: و عزل قطفير ثم مات بعد فزوجه الملك امرأته فلما دخل عليها قال أليس هذا خيرا مما طلبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During seven famine years Joseph sold grain successively for money, jewelry, livestock, slaves, property, children, and finally the Egyptians’ own persons; he freed them afterward and restored their property.
rows.anchor: وباع من أهل مصر فى سنين القحط الطعام بالدراهم والدنانير فى السنة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He limited each visitor to a camel-load, and famine also struck Canaan, so Jacob sent his sons to buy food, leading into the next verse.
rows.anchor: وكان لا يبيع لاحد من الممتارين اكثر من حمل بعير وأصاب ارض كنعان نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph recognized his brothers without their identifying themselves; they failed to recognize him because of changed clothing, a curtain, and the forty-year interval.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهم له منكرون ﴾ لتبدل الزي ولانه كان من وراء الحجاب ولطول المدة وهو اربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the brothers spoke Hebrew and claimed to be needy Syrian shepherds; Joseph suspected spies, and they swore they were sons of a grieving prophet whose lost son was dearer to him than the brother they brought.
rows.anchor: روى أنه لما رآهم وكلموه بالعبرانية قال لهم أخبرونى من أنتم وما شانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing their account, Joseph demanded that they bring the maternal brother if they were truthful.
rows.anchor: قالوا نحن قوم من أهل الشام رعاة أصابنا الجهد فجئنا نمتار فقال لعلكم جئتم عيونا تنظرون عورة بلادى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph gave each brother a camel-load of provisions; the qirāʾa with kasra on the jīm is anomalous.
rows.anchor: اعطى كل واحد منهم حمل بعير وقرئ بكسر الجيم شاذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awfī al-kayl means completing the measure; by praising his hospitality he encouraged them to return.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأنا خير المنزلين ﴾ كان قد أحسن إنزالهم وضيافتهم رغبهم بهذا الكلام على الرجوع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No more measure means Joseph will not sell them food; the phrase about not coming near continues the conditional jussive, or it may be a prohibition.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تقربون ﴾ أى فإن لم تأتونى به تحرموا ولا تقربوا فهو داخل فى حكم الجزاء مجزوم معطوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to coax and scheme until they obtain Benjamin from their father and insist they will not neglect the effort.
rows.anchor: تنزعه من يده ﴿ وإنا لفاعلون ﴾ ذلك لا محالة لا نفرط فيه ولا نتوانى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They left Simeon with Joseph, since Simeon had shown the best judgment concerning Joseph.
rows.anchor: قال فدعوا بعضكم هنا فتركوا عنده شمعون وكان أحسنهم رأيا فى يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufans except Abu Bakr read li-fityānihi; the others read li-fatīyatihi. Both are plurals of fatā, with one form for a few and one for many; the servants were the weighers.
rows.anchor: كوفى غير أبى بكر لفتيته غيرهم وهما جمع فتى كأخوة واخوان فى اخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden goods may have been sandals, leather, or silver; silver is more fitting to conceal in baggage.
rows.anchor: وكانت نعالا أو أدما أو ورقا وهو أليق بالدس فى الرحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By finding their money returned, they might recognize the generosity of receiving both the provisions and their payment back.
rows.anchor: يعرفون حق ردها وحق التكرم باعطاء البدلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their discovery when unloading could prompt their return; alternatively, they might have no payment left for another visit, or their piety would make them restore what was entrusted.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم ﴾ وفرغوا ظروفهم ﴿ لعلهم يرجعون ﴾ لعل معرفتهم بذلك تدعوهم إلى الرجوع إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Joseph did not consider it generous to take payment from his father and brothers.
rows.anchor: أو لم ير من الكرم أن يأخذ من أبيه واخوته ثمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that they were denied the measure refers to Joseph’s warning that he would withhold food unless Benjamin came; a threat of denial effectively denied it.
rows.anchor: يريدون قول يوسف فإن لم تأتون به فلا كيل لكم عندى لأنهم إذا أنذروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naktal means they would remove the obstacle to measuring and get their needed food; Hamza and Kisai read yaktal, making Benjamin’s measure join theirs.
rows.anchor: نرفع المانع من الكيل ونكتل من الطعام ما نحتاج إليه يكتل حمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They repeat their assurance that they will protect Benjamin from harm.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإنا له لحافظون ﴾ عن أن يناله مكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob recalls their previous promise about Joseph and says their assurance concerning Benjamin cannot be trusted after they betrayed their earlier pledge.
rows.anchor: يعنى انكم قلتم فى يوسف أرسله معنا غذا يرتع ويلعب و أنا له لحافظون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufans except Abu Bakr read ḥāfiẓan, parsed as circumstantial or specification; others read ḥifẓan, only as specification.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فالله خير حافظا ﴾ كوفى غير أبى بكر فتوكل على الله فيه ودفعه اليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob hopes God will preserve Benjamin and spare him a second calamity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهو أرحم الراحمين ﴾ فأرجو أن ينعم على بحفظه ولا يجمع على مصيبتين

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says God swore to restore both sons when Jacob said God is the best keeper.
rows.anchor: قال كعب لما قال فالله خير حفظا قال الله تعالى وعزتى وجلالى لاردن عليك كليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā nabghī can deny that they are going beyond the truth, mean they seek nothing beyond the kindness shown, or say they want no further provisions; it can also ask what more they could want.
rows.anchor: ما للنفى أى ما نبغى فى القول ولا نتجاوز الحق أو ما نبغي شيئا وراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that their payment was returned explains what they mean; the following statements connect to it, and the returned money can serve as capital.
rows.anchor: جملة مستأنفة موضحة لقوله ما نبغى والجمل بعدها معطوفة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Namīru means bringing provisions from another place; they will protect Benjamin and gain one more camel-load by taking him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ونمير أهلنا ﴾ فى رجوعنا إلى الملك أى نجلب لهم ميرة وهى طعام يحمل من غير بلدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A camel-load is easy for the ruler to provide.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذلك كيل يسير ﴾ سهل عليه متيسر لا يتعاظمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawthiq is a binding covenant from God, meaning an oath in His name; swearing by God reinforces pledges and is authorized by Him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ موثقا ﴾ عهدا ﴿ من الله ﴾ والمعنى حتى تعطونى ما اتوثق به من عند الله اي أراد أن يحلفوا له بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Makkan reading uses yāʾ in the form meaning that they bring Benjamin.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال لن أرسله معكم حتى تؤتون ﴾ وبالياء مكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La-taʾtunnanī is the answer to the oath; the exception means only overwhelming defeat can keep them from bringing him, so the affirmative promise must be understood as a negative for the exception to work.
rows.anchor: جواب اليمين لأن المعنى حتى تحلفوا لتأتننى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the brothers swore by God, Lord of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قيل حلفوا بالله رب محمد عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pausing after qāla separates the statement from its quotation incorrectly; a change in vocal force at Allah is preferable.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال ﴾ بعضهم يسكت عليه لأن المعنى قال يعقوب ﴿ الله على ما نقول ﴾ من طلب الموثق واعطائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most interpreters say Jacob feared the evil eye because the brothers were handsome and distinguished.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على أنه خاف عليهم العين لحمالهم وجلالة أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil eye is real: God may create a loss or defect when someone looks at a thing with admiration; the Prophet used a protective prayer for Hasan and Husayn.
rows.anchor: فالعين حق عندنا ووجه بان يحدث الله تعالى عند النظر إلى الشيء والاعجاب به نقصانا فيه وخللا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi denied the evil eye, but the author rejects his view on the preceding grounds and prophetic report.
rows.anchor: وأنكر الجبائى العين وهو مردود بما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that Jacob wanted to keep enemies from noticing the brothers and plotting to kill them.
rows.anchor: وقيل أنه أحب أن لا يفطن بهم أعداؤهم فيحتالوا لاهلاكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His precautions cannot counter God’s decree; tawakkul means entrusting the matter to God and relying on Him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما أغني عنكم من الله من شيء ﴾ أى أن كان الله أراد بكم سوءا لم ينفعكم ولم يدفع عنكم ما أشرت به عليكم من التفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering by separate gates could not avert God’s decree: they were accused of theft, Benjamin was detained, and their father’s grief grew.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما كان يغني عنهم ﴾ دخولهم من ابواب متفرقة ﴿ من الله من شيء ﴾ أى شيئا قط حيث أصابهم ماساءهم مع تفرقهم من إضافة السرقة اليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected: their entry only fulfilled Jacob’s concern for them.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي ولكن حاجة ﴿ في نفس يعقوب قضاها ﴾ وهي شفقته عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knew that caution cannot overcome destiny because God taught him; most people do not know this.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإنه لذو علم ﴾ يعنى قوله ما اعنى عنكم وعلمه بأن القدر لا يغنى عنه الحذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Benjamin was left alone at dinner, Joseph sat and ate with him; when Benjamin wished for Joseph as a brother, Joseph revealed himself and embraced him.
rows.anchor: فبقى بنيامين وحده فبكى وقال لو كان أخي يوسف حيا لأجلسنى معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph tells Benjamin not to grieve over their brothers’ past actions because God has treated them well and reunited them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فلا تبتئس ﴾ فلا تحزن ﴿ بما كانوا يعملون ﴾ بنا فيما مضى فان الله قد أحسن إلينا وجمعنا على خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Benjamin pleaded not to be separated from Joseph; Joseph said their father’s grief would deepen if Benjamin stayed, so he proposed hiding the cup and accusing him of theft, to which Benjamin agreed.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه قال له فأنا لا أفارقك قال لقد علمت اغتمام والدى بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After preparing and measuring their provisions, Joseph put the siqāya in Benjamin’s pack; it was a drinking cup used by the king, later used as a measure in the famine, and resembled a gold or silver bowl.
rows.anchor: السقاية هى مشربة يسقي بها وهي الصواع قيل كان يسقي بها الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A caller announced the theft; the root of adhāna means to make known and is especially well known because a caller does this often.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم أذن مؤذن ﴾ ثم نادى مناد آذنه أي أعلمه وأذن أكثر الأعلام ومنه المؤذن لكثرة ذلك منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the brothers had already departed when Joseph ordered them pursued and detained.
rows.anchor: روى انهم ارتحلوا وأمهلهم يوسف عليه السلام حتى انطلقوا ثم أمر بهم فادركوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿīr means camels carrying loads because they go and return; the address refers to the caravan’s people, and the accusation alludes to their having stolen Joseph from his father.
rows.anchor: هي الإبل التى عليها الاحمال لأنها تعير اي تذهب وتجىء والمراد اصحاب العير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The missing suwāʿ al-malik is the king’s sāʿ measure; the caller guarantees a camel-load of food for whoever brings it.
rows.anchor: قالوا نفقد صواع الملك ﴾ هو الصاع ﴿ ولمن جاء به حمل بعير وأنا به زعيم ﴾ يقوله المؤذن يريد وأنا بحمل البعير كفيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by God conveys astonishment at the accusation.
rows.anchor: قسم فيه معنى التعجب مما أضيف إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They appeal to the Egyptians’ knowledge of their honesty: their pack animals’ mouths were tied to prevent them eating others’ crops or food, and they had returned the money found in their packs.
rows.anchor: دخلوا وأفواه رواحلهم مشدودة لئلا تتناول زرعا أو طعاما لأحد من أهل السوق ولأنهم ردوا بضاعتهم التي وجدها في رحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny having ever been known as thieves.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما كنا سارقين ﴾ وما كنا نوصف قط بالسرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in jazāʾuhu refers to the cup; they ask what punishment follows if the brothers lied in denying the theft.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قالوا فما جزاؤه ﴾ الضمير للصواع أي فما جزاء سرقته ﴿ إن كنتم كاذبين ﴾ في جحودكم وادعاؤكم البراءة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under Jacob’s family law, a thief was enslaved for a year, which explains why the brothers were asked to state the penalty.
rows.anchor: وكان حكم السارق في آل يعقوب ان يسترق سنة فلذلك استفتوا في جزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-huwa jazāʾuhu either states that the offender himself is the punishment, or is the predicate of the conditional sentence.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فهو جزاؤه ﴾ تقرير للحكم أي فأخذ السارق نفسه هو جزاؤه لا غير أو جزاؤه مبتدأ والجملة الشرطية كما هي خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general claim about punishing wrongdoers means enslaving thieves.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كذلك نجزي الظالمين ﴾ أي السراق بالاسترقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph searched the other brothers’ baggage first to eliminate suspicion; they insisted he search Benjamin’s pack too for their own peace of mind.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بتفتيش أوعيتهم قبل وعاء بنيامين لنفي التهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in istakhrajahā refers to the cup; its feminine form reflects siqāya or the fact that ṣuwāʿ can be feminine as well as masculine.
rows.anchor: ذكر ضمير الصواع مرات ثم أنثه لأن التأنيث يرجع إلى السقاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kathālika refers to this clever stratagem, which God taught Joseph; the king’s law required double repayment rather than enslavement, so Joseph could not take Benjamin under that law.
rows.anchor: الكاف في ﴿ كذلك ﴾ في محل النصب أي مثل ذلك الكيد العظيم ﴿ كدنا ليوسف ﴾ يعنى علمناه إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph could retain his brother only by God’s will; God raises whom He chooses in knowledge, and above every learned person is the all-knowing God.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك ﴾ تفسير للكيد وبيان له لأن الحكم في دين الملك أي في سيرته للسارق أن يغرم مثلى ما أخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers accuse Joseph of stealing an idol from a temple and burying it; another report says he gave a household hen to a beggar.
rows.anchor: قيل دخل كنيسة فأخذ تمثالا صغيرا من ذهب كانوا يعبدونه فدفنه وقيل كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another story says Joseph’s aunt, who had adopted and loved him, hid Abraham’s heirloom belt under his clothes when Jacob sought to take him; she claimed the belt was lost, found it on Joseph, and kept him as her servant until her death.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانت منطقة لابراهيم عليه السلام يتوارثها أكابر ولده فورثها إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the ashamed brothers blamed Benjamin after the cup was found; he answered that they had taken Joseph and planted the cup in his baggage just as someone had returned their payment to theirs.
rows.anchor: وروى أنهم لما استخرجوا الصاع من رحل بنيامين نكس اخوته رءوسهم حياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph concealed their accusation as if he had not heard it; he said silently that they were in a worse position because they stole him from his father.
rows.anchor: قال أنتم شر مكانا ﴾ تمييز أي أنتم شر منزلة في السرق لأنكم سرقتم اخاكم يوسف من أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah knows what they say and whether it is true or a lie.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والله أعلم بما تصفون ﴾ تقولون أو تكذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob is called old in both age and standing; the brothers ask Joseph to take one of them as hostage or servant so their father may be comforted.
rows.anchor: في السن وفي القدر ﴿ فخذ أحدنا مكانه ﴾ ابدله على وجه الاسترهان أو الاستعباد فان اباه يتسلى به عن أخيه المفقود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their praise means either that Joseph should complete his kindness to them or continue his customary generosity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنا نراك من المحسنين ﴾ الينا فأتمم احسانك أو من عادتك الاحسان فاجر على عادتك ولا تغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿādh Allāh is a verbal noun meaning I seek refuge in God; it is annexed to its object, with the preposition min omitted.
rows.anchor: أي نعوذ بالله معاذا من ان نأخذ فأضيف المصدر إلى المفعول به وحذف من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking anyone but the person whose baggage held the cup would be unjust even by the brothers’ own ruling, so Joseph rebukes their request.
rows.anchor: لأن المعنى ان اخذنا بدله ظلمنا وهذا لأنه وجب على قضية فتواكم اخذ من وجد الصاع في رحله واستعباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istaʾyasū means they despaired; the sīn and tāʾ intensify the sense, as in istiʿṣama.
rows.anchor: يئسوا وزيادة السين والتاء للمبالغة كما مر في استعصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalasū means they withdrew from the others; najiy may mean people confiding, a group in private conversation, or the act of intense confidential discussion.
rows.anchor: انفردوا عن الناس خالصين لا يخالطهم سواهم ﴿ نجيا ﴾ ذوى نجوى أو فوجا نجيا اي مناجيا لمناجاة بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their consultation concerned what to do and tell their father; they deliberated with urgency as if they themselves embodied confidential speech.
rows.anchor: وكان تناجيهم في تدير أمرهم على أي صفة يذهبون وماذا يقولون لأبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eldest brother may be Reuben by age, Judah by intelligence and judgment, or Simeon as leader.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال كبيرهم ﴾ في السن وهو روبين أو في العقل والرأي وهو يهوذا أو رئيسهم وهو شمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In min qablu, mā may be extra, meaning they previously failed concerning Joseph, or a relative noun in a construction meaning their failure with Joseph occurred earlier.
rows.anchor: ما صلة أي ومن قبل هذا قصرتم في شأن يوسف ولم تحفظوا عهد أبيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: I will not leave Egypt until my father permits it, unless God rules that I leave, die, or fight the others; God judges with justice.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فلن أبرح الأرض ﴾ فلن أفارق أرض مصر ﴿ حتى يأذن لي أبي ﴾ في الانصراف اليه ﴿ أو يحكم الله لي ﴾ بالخروج منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading may be sariqa, your son stole, or suriqa, he was accused of stealing.
rows.anchor: وقرىء سرق أي نسب إلى السرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they testified only to what they knew because the cup was found in Benjamin’s baggage; they did not know he would steal when they gave the pledge.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما شهدنا ﴾ عليه بالسرقة ﴿ إلا بما علمنا ﴾ من سرقته وتيقنا إذ الصواع استخرج من وعائه ﴿ وما كنا للغيب حافظين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ask the village means ask Egypt’s people about what happened; the caravan means its people, who were Canaanites neighboring Jacob.
rows.anchor: يعنى مصر اي أرسل إلى أهلها فاسألهم عن كنه القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They insist they are telling the truth.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإنا لصادقون ﴾ في قولنا فرجعوا إلى ابيهم وقالوا له ما قال لهم أخوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob suspects they invented the story: how would the Egyptian know the thief’s punishment is enslavement if the brothers had not supplied the rule?
rows.anchor: أردتموه وإلا فمن أدرى ذلك الرجل أن السارق يسترق لو لا فتواكم وتعليمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob chooses beautiful patience and hopes God will return Joseph, Benjamin, and the eldest brother.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فصبر جميل عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعا ﴾ بيوسف وأخيه وكبيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows Jacob’s grief and sorrow and has wisdom in allowing this trial.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنه هو العليم ﴾ بحالى في الحزن والأسف ﴿ الحكيم ﴾ الذي لم يبتلنى بذلك إلا لحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob turned away because he disliked their news; his cry adds the intensified grief to himself, with alif replacing possessive yāʾ, and a natural sound-play pairs asaf with Yusuf.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتولى عنهم ﴾ واعرض عنهم كراهة لما جاءوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tafsir adduces assonant or rhyming pairs in other verses: iththāqaltum/arḍītum, yanhawna/yanʾawna, taḥsabūna/yuḥsinūna, and Sabaʾ/nabaʾ.
rows.anchor: ونحوه اثاقلتم إلى الأرض أرضيتم وهم ينهون عنه وينأون عنه وتحسبون انهم يحسنون صنعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob grieves for Joseph rather than Benjamin or the eldest because the older grief endured so long and remained fresh.
rows.anchor: وإنما تأسف على يوسف دون أخيه وكبيرهم لتمادى أسفه على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His eyes whitened after much weeping as tears erased their blackness; others say he became blind or could see only weakly.
rows.anchor: إذ أكثر الاستعبار ومحقت العبرة سواد العين وقلبته لى بياض كدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Jacob’s eyes did not dry for eighty years and that he was the most honored person on earth to God.
rows.anchor: قيل ما جفت عينا يعقوب من وقت فراق يوسف إلى حين لقائه ثمانين عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets may be overwhelmed by grief because people cannot control themselves then; Jacob is praised for patience, as the Prophet wept for his son Ibrahim but rejected words that anger God.
rows.anchor: ويجوز للنبي عليه السلام أن يبلغ به الجزع ذلك المبلغ لأن الإنسان مجبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blameworthy response is wailing, lamenting, striking the chest or face, and tearing clothes.
rows.anchor: وإنما المذموم الصياح والنياحة ولطم الصدور والوجوه وتمزيق الثياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kazīm means filled with grief and anger toward his sons but concealing it from them; the form is passive, supported by the description of Jonah as distressed, and comes from tying a full waterskin.
rows.anchor: أولاده ولا يظهر ما يسوءهم فعيل بمعنى مفعول بدليل قوله إذ نادى وهو مكظوم من كظم السقاء إذا شده على ملئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafteʾu means you will not cease; the negative particle is omitted because it cannot be mistaken, since an affirmative would require the lām and nūn.
rows.anchor: أي لا تفتأ فحذف حرف النفي لأنه لا يلتبس إذ لو كان إثباتا لم يكن بد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaraḍan means sick and close to death; the alternative is that Jacob will become one of the dead.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تذكر يوسف حتى تكون حرضا ﴾ مشفيا على الهلاك مرضا
